item.title: I solved 823 LeetCode problems by age 18. Here is why LeetCode is broken
item.summary: I’m 18, and I’ve recently solved my 823rd problem on LeetCode with a 430+ day streak. After a year of doing this every single day, I can confidently tell you: LeetCode is a dry platform for micro-optimization, and it has almost nothing to do with real software education. It shouldn't, but it's a problem. The biggest flaw is the learning loop. When you encounter a new architectural or algorithmic concept, you are forced to break your flow. You have to leave the platform, read abstract documentation, watch a 3-hour YouTube video, or sift through AI slop. By the time you return to the editor, you've experienced massive context switching. This applies to tech education as a whole: we find information, read it, take notes, and then never look at those notes again because passive re-reading is boring. As a result, we forget most of it. I wanted to fix this feedback loop for myself and others. I built Self University — a platform that turns everything you can be asked in an engineering interview into an interactive puzzle that you assemble by hand. It features a massive knowledge graph covering hundreds of puzzles across networking, databases, cloud native, backend cores, frontend perform
